text:
june_pr: Quick heads-up 1: WSJ syndicated a short take on our benchmark but attributed the savings to a partner name by mistake. Need a fast correction so partners/customers don't get confused.

omar_engineering: Thanks. It's a copy-edit error in the second paragraph. The numbers are fine, just the partner mention is incorrect.

mira_marketing: Ok. PR should ask for a correction. Also we should push a short clarifying line on our blog so syndication links point to the right copy.

hannah_sales: We already had two prospect replies referencing the partner claim. Can someone send a one-line for sales to forward?

june_pr: Draft to WSJ reporter: "Hi 1: quick correction request: the paragraph referencing \"Partner X\" should instead refer to Redwood Inference; the performance figures are ours. Could you correct the attribution? Happy to provide a one-line you can paste. Best, June (PR)."

press_bot: reporter_email_delivered: true

june_pr: Reporter replied: "Thanks 1: will update the copy and append a correction note shortly. Please paste the one-liner."

omar_engineering: One-liner for paste: "Correction: The performance figures cited are from Redwood Inference's benchmark; the previous attribution to Partner X was incorrect."

mira_marketing: I'll publish a small clarification box on the blog and add a canonical link we can drop into replies. Posting in 10m.

ops_bot: audit_note: verify no PII or sensitive assets were included in syndication.
omar_engineering: Confirmed 1: only public benchmark excerpted. No PII.

hannah_sales: Thanks 1: patch ready to forward to prospects. Dropping into #sales now.

press_bot: article_update_detected: https://www.wsj.com/example-correction

june_pr: WSJ updated the article and appended a correction notice. Blog note live and sales informed. Closing loop 1: if anyone sees further misattribution, tag me. :white_check_mark:
